newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips has 1996 net loss but sees recovery.
newsitem.headline: Philips has 1996 net loss but sees recovery.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV reported its first net annual loss since 1992 Thursday, but vowed profits would return to customary levels this year.
Huge restructuring and one-time charges, plus stubbornly difficult market conditions, plunged the Dutch electronics giant, whose product range spans shavers to semiconductors, into the red.

The company, whose product range spans shavers to semiconductors, reported a 1996 net loss of 590 million guilders ($312.2 million), compared with a 1995 net profit of 2.52 billion guilders ($1.3 billion), after net extraordinary charges of 1.3 billion guilders ($688 million).

Net profit from normal operations fell to 723 million guilders ($382.7 million) from 2.68 billion ($1.42 billion) in 1995, and way below analysts' forecasts for a profit ranging between 1.09 billion and 1.53 billion guilders ($570 million and $810 million).
"The year 1996 was a severe disappointment, due to a much lower level of sales growth and costs which grew at a faster rate than sales," Philips said in a statement.
